display_title_he: סקיידאנס משלימה מיזוג ענק בתעשיית המדיה
short_summary: Skydance has finalized a $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating a new media powerhouse led by David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz.

sources.name: Walla
sources.title: מפלצת של 110 מיליארד דולר: המספרים מאחורי עסקת השנה בהוליווד

paragraphs: The global entertainment landscape has undergone a seismic shift following the completion of a $110 billion merger between Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery. This monumental transaction places David Ellison at the helm of one of the world's most influential media and news conglomerates, uniting legendary franchises such as 'Mission: Impossible,' 'Harry Potter,' and DC Studios under a single corporate umbrella. The newly formed entity, operating as Skydance, has transitioned its stock listing from the Nasdaq to the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol 'SKYD.'

Ellison has articulated a vision for a next-generation media firm, emphasizing that the merger is designed to compete directly with industry titans like Netflix and Disney, as well as technology giants including Apple, Amazon, and Meta. The transition follows the resolution of complex legal hurdles involving various U.S. states and the Writers Guild of America. To manage the immense operational challenges, Ellison has appointed Ynon Kreiz, the former CEO of Mattel, as co-CEO. While Ellison focuses on creative strategy and long-term vision, Kreiz is tasked with overseeing day-to-day operations and achieving a targeted $6 billion in cost savings. Much of this efficiency is expected to come from consolidating technology and cloud service providers, though analysts warn that significant job cuts across the industry are likely inevitable.

The company faces a daunting financial reality, including a massive debt load of approximately $80 billion. To address this, the leadership plans to merge the HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming services and has committed to a robust production schedule, aiming to release at least 30 films annually over the next two years, with plans to increase that number to 32 thereafter. Ellison has pledged to invest at least $30 billion annually into content development to maintain market relevance. Projections suggest the company's core operating profit could reach $16 billion by 2028, rising to $19 billion by 2030.

Despite skepticism from some Wall Street analysts regarding the scale of the debt and the consolidation of power, Ellison remains focused on the broader industry context. He argues that the merger is a necessary evolution in an era where traditional Hollywood models are challenged by shifting consumer habits, the rise of artificial intelligence, and the decline of cable television subscriptions. The deal has received notable support from U.S. President Donald Trump, who described the merger as a positive development. As the company moves forward, the success of this integration will depend on its ability to balance the creative legacy of its studios with the rigorous financial demands of the modern digital age.

facts.fact: Skydance has completed the acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in a deal valued at $110 billion.
The merged entity, operating under the name Skydance, will be traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol 'SKYD'.
David Ellison serves as CEO, with Ynon Kreiz appointed as co-CEO to manage operations.
The company aims to merge streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+ while targeting $6 billion in cost savings.
The deal includes a massive debt load of approximately $80 billion.
